discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the opening of neutrino astronomy with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived, championed and led the construction of IceCube, a cubic-kilometre neutrino telescope in the Antarctic ice, growing it out of the pioneering AMANDA experiment. In 2013 IceCube reported the first diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, a clear excess over atmospheric backgrounds established through careful statistical analysis. The detection of a neutrino coincident with the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017), evidence for neutrino emission from NGC 1068 (2022), and the observation of neutrinos from the Galactic plane (2023) turned this into a new window on the universe. Neutrinos travel unimpeded from the densest, most energetic cosmic environments, so this work gives a probe of cosmic-ray acceleration and fundamental neutrino physics at energies no accelerator can reach. Like earlier messenger-opening discoveries, it came from building an entirely new observational capability and following it through with rigour.
